signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Safe-Haven vs Strait of Hormuz Escalation
signals.text: Trump's weekend rhetoric regarding the Strait of Hormuz as U.S. territory alongside Iranian defiance shifts market focus toward safe-haven JPY demand for the Sydney open. JPY COT net short -59,526 (35.3% long) creates significant short-squeeze risk as USD/JPY closed at 159.31 Friday, pressured by weak U.S. retail sales and a negative ESI of -14.4. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 62% hike priced) and potential yen-positive headlines on geopolitical risk resolve the current yield-carry dominance of 264bp in favor of USD. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY on geopolitical escalation; JPY short-covering risk is elevated. Catalyst: Sydney open response to Strait of Hormuz headlines. Risk: De-escalation or U.S. yield spike above 4.70% restores the carry bid.

signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Energy Disruption Bid
signals.text: CAD is the G10 leader with a 1W avg +1.064% (n=3) while JPY laggard status at -1.018% (n=7) creates a 2.083% spread, the strongest bilateral theme in the G10. Oil prices closed Friday up +1.42% at $82.4 as Iran continues to disrupt vessel traffic, providing a fundamental tailwind for CAD alongside its moderate positive ESI of +13.3. CAD/JPY carry of +125bp supports the long-CAD bias, though JPY's safe-haven status in a geopolitical flare-up acts as a late-session offset. Trade bias: Bullish CAD/JPY into the open; CAD momentum is supported by oil and data beats. Catalyst: Tokyo open response to WTI crude volatility. Risk: Broad risk-off sentiment triggers a JPY safe-haven reversal and CAD/JPY carry unwind.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning vs Domestic ESI Weakness
signals.text: AUD COT LF long +45,727 (74.6% long) creates a crowded-long unwind risk even as AUD/USD closed Friday at 0.7087 with a -73bp OIS carry advantage over USD. Despite the carry bid, Australia's negative ESI of -11.1 suggests data is consistently disappointing, while retail sentiment is heavily short at 80%, providing a contrarian cap on further gains. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 29 Sep is the primary event that determines if the hold bias can sustain the current bid against positioning extremes. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD; crowded speculative longs limit upside despite favorable carry. Catalyst: Sydney open response to Friday's DXY weakness. Risk: Sustained DXY slide below 99.00 forces further AUD/USD short-covering.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Exhaustion at Multi-Month Highs
signals.text: GBP COT LF net long +42,722 (71.9% long) signals extreme positioning as British Pound futures hit 3-month highs following UK GDP data. While GBP/USD closed Friday at 1.3536 with a mild -11bp OIS carry advantage, the high 75% retail short sentiment and 5.0% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.0%) reflect heavy hedging demand for downside protection. The next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) is the catalyst for confirming if the real policy rate of +0.93% can attract fresh buyers to challenge the 1.3600 handle. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD on positioning exhaustion; high spec longs face liquidation if USD recovers. Catalyst: Sydney open response to DXY holding 99.50 support. Risk: UK inflation beats next week force a hawkish BoE pivot.

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Hike Bias vs Negative ESI Lag
signals.text: EUR COT net short -77,671 (32.6% long) remains the largest G10 speculative short, providing fuel for a short-squeeze as ECB holds at 2.4%. EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.1573 but carries a significant -144bp OIS disadvantage against USD, which is likely to limit the pair's ability to capitalize on DXY weakness. The mild real policy rate of +0.09% in the Eurozone vs USD +1.52% maintains a structural headwind for EUR upside. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD on short-covering; extreme COT shorts are vulnerable to further USD weakness. Catalyst: Sydney open response to U.S. retail sales miss. Risk: ECB shifts to a dovish hold bias in communications before Sep 10.
